objective: Replay the frozen M122 held-out workload and charge the interface cycles and descriptor traffic omitted by the ideal K4 fold model.
paper_safe_statement: On the frozen held-out module workload, explicitly charging one row-mask admission cycle per active row-block raises M125/M127 candidate cycles to 446,132,870, while conservative descriptor startup gives M128 351,479,358 cycles, a 1.2693x module-cycle advantage. M128's 53-bit payload is 1.2696x the row-mask traffic, so no bandwidth, physical, system, energy, or headline claim is admitted.
prohibited_claims: Do not call the 1.2693x module-cycle comparison an end-to-end system speedup.
Do not claim M128 reduces descriptor bandwidth.
Do not treat the proposed 35-bit M130 format as implemented or verified evidence.
Do not multiply this cycle ratio by frequency before a matched Synopsys period grid and independent review.
Do not infer SRAM or DRAM energy from payload bit counts.
